examples.text: The environment is dynamic, changing with the years and the seasons.

glosses: Having to do with the volume of sound.

examples.text: The dynamic marking in bar 40 is forte.

glosses: Happening at runtime instead of being predetermined at compile time.

examples.text: the dynamic resizing of an array

glosses: Pertaining to dynamics, the branch of mechanics concerned with the effects of forces on the motion of objects.
Of a verb: not stative, but fientive; indicating continued or progressive action on the part of the subject.
A characteristic or manner of an interaction; a behavior.

examples.text: Watch the dynamic between the husband and wife when they disagree.
One of the under-reported dynamics during the coronavirus pandemic has been the collapse of One Nation’s vote.
The study of fluid dynamics quantifies turbulent and laminar flows.

glosses: The varying loudness or volume of a song or the markings that indicate the loudness.

examples.text: If you pay attention to the dynamics as you play, it's a very moving piece.

glosses: A symbol in a musical score that indicates the desired level of volume.
A verb that indicates continued or progressive action on the part of the subject.
